title: Emmett Hardy and Bix's influences
summary: Discussion of Emmett Hardy, the lost cylinder, and who influenced Bix's sound.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: followed that style. In other words, you can listen to his records and see that the pattern of the Dixieland music and the Rhythm Kings and the Walden's music was there, excepting that he used his own ideas, his solos and his phrasing and things like that, which you couldn't say that that was anything wrong, excepting that it was a great new sound.
Well, Herman, where shall we place Emmett Hardy in relation to Bix?

Emmett Hardy, John, that's something I have heard of. I've often wondered about it. How can you tell? What can you say? I didn't know him. No one had a recording of him, did they? I don't think so, did they? I never found him. They said, Monk Hazel said there was a cylinder disc that was made of him, but no one has ever really found it. And Monk Hazel, who I dearly loved as a friend and as a musician, I think Monk really, really knew what he was talking about when he told you something. And Monk said that he thought that Emmett sounded a lot like Bix. He always said that. He used to always tell me that. And of course, a lot of people said, well, I just don't believe that anybody sounded like Bix. You know, in other words, it could have been possible. That someone would have sounded like Bix before Bix, let's put it that way. Before Bix. And this was Monk's contention that somewhere along the line, Bix had heard Emmett Hardy. Now, whether or not this is so, I could say. But it's a thought and it's something to think about. Because once again, it would be a great thing if we had known for certain that Emmett Hardy had really had any influence on Bix. Because somewhere along the line, someone has always had an influence on someone. Right, Bill?
We know definitely that King Oliver influenced Louis. And others before King Oliver influenced him. It went on down the line, you see. But who did influence Bix with that sound?

Well, I guess a lot of musicians who have played with Hardy, I guess Ray Burt was one that played with him early. But I forgot what interview it was. They were talking about his sound being the pure New Orleans sound, but with a sweet tone that was not characteristic of New Orleans sound. But they say that Buddy Molden, too.
